title: AuroraOps - Concurrency SLAs & eviction tolerance intake
summary: Initial intake focused on reserved GPU sizing, tenant eviction/prekemptible tolerance, concurrency targets for low-latency endpoints and tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer has a mixed batch/interactive workload, strong constraints on multi-tenant isolation, and wants a fail-open fallback strategy. Discussed SOC2/KMS needs and an internal perf spreadsheet they'd like Redwood to run a short benchmark against.
topics: preemption / eviction tolerance and warm pool strategy
burst strategy vs reserved capacity sizing
data residency, KMS and audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-04 16:00 UTC · 45m
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (AuroraOps Platform Lead), Priya Patel (AuroraOps SRE), Daniel Kim (CTO - joined 16:30), Maya (engineer)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for blocking time. uh quick intros, and then we can dive into your traffic patterns.
[00:18] Alex (AuroraOps): Hey all, Alex here. We're the infra team for AuroraOps, we run GKE clusters across us-west and eu-west. we have a mix of batch embedding jobs and interactive chat completions.
[00:30] Priya: Yep, and our biggest pain right now is that when spot nodes go away, our latency spikes and we lose warm kv cash — sorry kv cache — so cold starts kill us.
[00:45] Marcus (Redwood): Mm-hmm, so you mentioned both batch and interactive, do you have numbers for RPS or tokens/sec at peak?
[01:05] Alex: Ballpark: interactive is about 120 qps at peak across regions, embeddings batch peaks at like 40 concurrent jobs which is heavy GPU time. Tokens are variable but interactive tends to be 1k-2k tokens per request.
[01:28] Sofia: Got it. And what's your SLO today? p95, p99 targets?
[01:35] Priya: We aim for p95 < 300ms for the user path that matters (small prompts), p99 < 900ms ideally, but that p99 is the thing that breaks when preemption happens.
[01:50] Marcus: Ok, this is exactly the kind of profile where Dedicated reserved GPU pools can help — predictable throughput, isolation. But there are tradeoffs w/ cost. Are you considering Hosted first or do you need Private/VPC for data governance?
[02:10] Alex: Data residency & KMS matter to us. Some workloads need our KMS, so Private / VPC or on-prem path is required eventually. But we might pilot on Dedicated hosted with a VPC tunnel, if that's possible.
[02:29] Sofia: Yes we support Private with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. For Dedicated hosted we can also offer a dedicated pool with restricted tenancy and audit logs.
[02:40] Priya: Important question: how do you handle evictions/preemption? If our node gets preempted mid-inference, do you have graceful fallback to a cheaper model? or do requests just fail?
[02:55] Marcus: Good question. Redwood runtime has smart routing and automatic fallback policies — so you can set a policy to route to a smaller quantized model or a hosted variant in another region. We also do prefix/KV cache reuse where possible, but there are limits on resumable streams when preemption occurs.
[03:18] Alex: And what about Kubernetes-level eviction — like pod eviction because of node pressure? we use GKE autoscaler — how does Redwood integrate?
[03:30] Marcus: We have a couple of options: 1) dedicate nodes to reserved pools (no preemption) 2) use warm pools / prewarmed containers in a hotpool to reduce cold start 3) use opportunistic nodes for burst with fallback. For k8s autoscaling we surface metrics and hooks — but sometimes eviction still causes you to lose KV cache.
[03:55] Priya: So if we pick reserved GPUs, is the expectation that pods never get preempted? like guaranteed in the contract?
[04:05] Sofia: Reserved capacity gives you reserved GPU allocation in our infra. For dedicated on-prem we can give you fully customer-owned nodes. For hosted Dedicated, we provide SLA on availability and isolation but preemption for spot-style nodes isn't part of reserved pools. We'll include eviction tolerances in the contract.
[04:28] Alex: Cool. Timeline question — we'd like to pilot in 4 weeks, run a soak for two weeks, then decide on annual reserved. Does that timeline sound realistic?
[04:40] Marcus: Yes, typical pilot is 2–6 weeks. We'll do a performance benchmark and a small canary rollout.
[04:47] Sofia: Can we get a quick sense of what success looks like?
[04:51] Alex: Success = p95 < 300ms under baseline load, p99 < 900ms under sustained load, ability to survive an eviction window (injecting node loss) with automatic fallback and less than 1% error rate on user queries. Also cost per 1k tokens under $X — we'll share internal target.
[05:12] Priya: Also auditors will want SOC2 artifacts, KMS alignment, and we need to map audit logs to our Splunk instance.
[05:22] Marcus: We have SOC2, we can export audit logs, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. We'll attach the security pack after the call.
[05:32] Daniel (CTO, joined): Hey quick FYI, we also evaluate competitors on how they handle multi-tenant noisy neighbor mitigation, i.e. tenant fencing and QoS.
[05:43] Sofia: Understood. We expose tenant fencing policies and can limit burst by tenant.
[05:50] Alex: A few technical clarifying questions — Marcus, you mentioned prefix caching. Does the runtime support KV cache warmup across restarts? We get cache misses when pods move.
[06:05] Marcus: We persist KV cache for short windows and can snapshot caches to a warm pool. But if a pod's presence is lost to node preemption and the cache TTL elapsed, you will pay a cold penalty. We can recommend cache TTL settings based on your workload.
[06:24] Maya (Dev): What about batching? Our embedding jobs could benefit but chat needs low latency.
[06:30] Marcus: We do continuous batching with latency SLO-aware thresholds; for chat endpoints you can opt out of batching or set very small batch windows. For embeddings we maximize throughput.
[06:45] Alex: For reserved sizing: how do we estimate number of GPUs for 120 qps interactive?
[06:52] Marcus: Rough rule: estimate tokens/sec per GPU for the model variant. If using an Llama-style 13B quantized, you might get ~60–80 qps per A100 equiv for small prompts; for large tokens it'll be lower. We'll run exact sims during the pilot against your prompts.
[07:16] Priya: Are you able to run a chaos/injection test during the pilot where we kill nodes to validate fallback?
[07:24] Marcus: Absolutely. Our recommended pilot includes a resilience test where we simulate node preemption and verify fallback to a compatible variant or region.
[07:33] Alex: Network egress — if we go Private on VPC, how do you handle egress for model downloads and for telemetry? Need to keep traffic internal where possible.
[07:45] Sofia: Private deployments can control model artifacts fetching; we can support air-gapped model bundles for on-prem. Telemetry can be streamed to your Splunk over private peering.
[07:56] Priya: Ok. On security: KMS — we need to use our Cloud KMS, not Redwood's. Is that supported?
[08:04] Marcus: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and for Dedicated with the appropriate contract. We also support HSM integrations for enterprise.
[08:14] Daniel: Cost modeling — we need a concrete cost-per-1k tokens for each config: Hosted dedicated, Private on-prem, and hybrid.
[08:25] Sofia: We'll send a benchmark cost spreadsheet. Marcus: we'll also include quantization and batching knobs for cost modeling.
[08:33] Alex: One weird gotcha: some of our endpoints are sensitive to latency tail — we sometimes see p99 spikes when eviction happens, but also when a heavy batch job runs. Can you guarantee isolation so batch doesn't affect chat?
[08:49] Marcus: With dedicated pools and tenant fencing you can isolate batch onto separate nodes or pools with QoS limits. We recommend separate pools: one dedicated hotpool for chat, another for batch.
[09:03] Priya: If we do a hybrid approach (some on-prem + Redwood dedicated in cloud) how does routing work? Can you route by policy to lowest-latency region or to on-prem first?
[09:14] Marcus: Smart routing policies support region, cost, and model variant rules. You can prefer on-prem when healthy and fallback to cloud Dedicated otherwise.
[09:25] Alex: Any limitations around GPU types? We use NVIDIA A10G in our fleet currently.
[09:31] Marcus: We support a variety of Nvidia GPUs; some models are tuned per-kernel. For peak latency we recommend A100 or H100 class; but we can run tuning on A10G too. Performance profile will be model and sequence-length dependent.
[09:51] Sofia: Quick note — auditors will ask about retention on logs and transcripts. We can do custom retention policies.
[10:00] Alex: Great. Let's talk about pilot steps — what exactly will you deliver in the 2-week pilot?
[10:07] Marcus: Pilot outline: 1) onboarding + enclave setup (VPC peering), 2) baseline perf runs with your prompt set, 3) resilience injection (node kill, preemption), 4) report + recommended reserved sizing + cost model.
[10:25] Priya: For onboarding what access do you need to our cluster? We prefer minimal privileges.
[10:31] Marcus: We can do API-only integration for metrics, and use a temporary service account for canary nodes if you want deeper telemetry. We'll provide step-by-step infra checklist.
[10:43] Maya: Who will run the benchmarks — Redwood or AuroraOps?
[10:47] Marcus: Redwood can run them if you provide the prompt sets and sample inputs. We also supply a harness so you can re-run locally.
[10:55] Alex: Ok. Regarding compliance docs, can you share SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide?
[11:00] Sofia: Yes, will attach SOC2 cert and security pack.
[11:05] [Speaker 2 — mislabel]: So about tenancy: can we throttle per-tenant at the API gateway?
[11:12] Marcus: Yes, per-tenant throttling and token quotas are supported; we can also enforce burst caps at the router.
[11:20] Alex: For SLA, what does Redwood commit to in terms of replacement capacity if a reserved node fails?
[11:27] Sofia: Our Dedicated SLA includes time-to-replace metrics and options for burst capacity to compensate during failures. We'll include concrete numbers in the contract draft.
[11:40] Priya: Very important for us: p99 under a simulated 10% node loss must remain below 1s for chat. Is that a reasonable ask?
[11:51] Marcus: We can tune routing to satisfy that in most cases; it'll depend on model size and token lengths. We'll test it in the pilot.
[12:00] Alex: Also, we'd like a test where you simulate a noisy neighbour — like saturating a tenant to see if fencing works.
[12:08] Marcus: Agreed, that's part of the chaos suite. We'll include tenant-fencing tests.
[12:15] Sofia: Quick admin — Daniel, do you want finance to be looped now or after pilot?
[12:20] Daniel: After pilot. We need numbers first.
[12:24] Alex: Any blockers you foresee?
[12:28] Marcus: No big blockers. We'll need prompt sets, access for benchmark runner, and a short list of endpoints to prioritize.
[12:36] Priya: Ok, let's assign action items.

[12:40] End of transcript section — call continued with scheduling notes and brief doc review.
action_items: Alex: Share canonical prompt set and QPS traces (due 2025-03-06)
Marcus: Run baseline perf on provided prompts and return benchmark spreadsheet (due 2025-03-14)
Sofia: Share SOC2 report, KMS integration guide, and Dedicated pricing template (due 2025-03-05)
Priya: Provide Splunk endpoint and log retention requirements (due 2025-03-07)
Daniel: Confirm finance contact post-pilot (no due date)
next_steps: Redwood to run pilot with perf + resilience tests (2-week window starting upon prompt set delivery)
Schedule a technical deep dive with SEs to review tuning knobs (Marcus to propose times)
Deliver cost-per-1k tokens model across Hosted dedicated, Private on-prem, and hybrid scenarios
